English translation:
1 [...]
1 [...] from the city of Oxyrhynchus. Since
2 Theon son of Pausiris, of
3 the same city of Oxyrhynchus, has served on me through the
4 strategus of the nome a copy of a memorandum, which he im-
5 properly had executed at the record office,
6 by which he made a demand for what he alleged
7 to be owed to him both by the maternal grandfather of my minor son
8 Sarapion, Sarapion,
9 and his brother Dionysius, from former
10 times, as capital sums of silver, I make the
11 proper counter-statement, declaring that I suspect that the security
12 of the loan which he claims to have existed has been discharged,
13 both because it is of long standing and because
14 Sarapion survived two years, and after his death
15 his daughter, who became my wife
16 and mother of the minor Sarapion, Eubu-
17 lia, likewise survived eleven years, and
18 after her death too another five years
19 passed, and Theon did not venture
20 to come forward; and further that Eubulia,
21 while she was alive, sold to the aforesaid
22 brother of Sarapion, Dionysius, property
23 of Sarapion for six talents of silver
24 and more, on condition that he should pay
25 Sarapion's creditors the debts owed by him,
26 and that Theon, being creditor of Sarapion for other
27 capital sums, recovered those
28 from Dionysius, but made no mention at all
29 of this one. Therefore I ask you to give orders to write to the strategus of the Oxyrhyn-
30 chite nome to serve on Theon a copy
31 of this memorandum, so that he may know
32 that the notice which he improperly served on me
33 is void, and to serve also whatever he may write in reply,
34 while my right to legal action against
35 him remains in matters where it is needed, I contenting
36 myself with this declaration, as is proper. Year 15
37 of Imperator Caesar Trajanus Hadrianus
38 Augustus, Epeiph 1. Signed, Epeiph 1.

Loan in ll. 6-12.
Date: about 18 years before the petition (AD 131): Sarapion lived 2 years after the loan, Eubulia 11 more, then 5 more years passed.
Place: not stated; the place of the document.

English translation:
1 ⳨ To my good master, lover of Christ, lover of the poor, all-
2 renowned, most magnificent patrician and dux of the Thebaid
3 region, Apion, from Anoup, your wretched slave, from the
4 estate belonging to it called Phakra.
5 The glorious house of my good master possesses nothing unjust or impious,
6 but is always full of mercy, pouring out to the needy
7 what they need. Therefore I too, the wretched slave of my good master,
8 through this present petition wish to be shown mercy,
9 (and) to make known to your lordship that from my fathers and forefathers I have served
10 my good master, paying the public taxes every year; and by God's
11 will, in the past eleventh indiction and the past
12 tenth my animals died, and I borrowed no little gold,
13 (15 solidi), until I could buy the same animals. But when I approached
14 my good master and (asked him) to have mercy on me, (and) came here, the agents
15 of my master would not consent to act according to the order of my good
16 master. For if, master, your mercy does not reach me, I cannot stand
17 on my holding and be useful to the landowner's affairs. And
18 I beseech and implore your lordship to order that mercy be shown
19 to me, since I have come to great ruin. For I have no other
20 refuge but that of the Lord Christ and of your eminence.
21 And I will send up undying hymns to the Lord Christ for the
22 life of your lordship and of its most magnificent son
23 Strategius, master. ⳨

Loan in ll. 11-13.
Date: after the animals died in the 10th and 11th indictions (AD 546-548), before the petition (AD 548/9?).
Place: not stated; the place of the document.

1 ⳨ In the reign of our most divine and most pious master Flavius Justinian, eternal Augustus
2 and Imperator, year 24, in the 8th (year) after the consulship of Flavius Basilius, vir clarissimus,
3 Phaophi 22, indiction 14, in the city of Oxyrhynchus. ⳨
4 To Flavius Apion, the all-renowned and most magnificent former consul ordinarius,
5 landowner also here in the splendid city of the Oxyrhynchites, through Menas, servant, who makes the stipulation
6 and acquires for his own master, the same all-renowned man, the right of action and
7 obligation, the community of the protokometai of the village of Takona of the Oxyrhynchite
8 nome, whose pagarchy is held by the house of your glory, through us, the Aurelii
9 Phoebammon, meizon, son of Pekysius, and Anoup son of Aritsi, and Menas his brother,
10 and Koulaetb son of Iohannes, and Anoup son of Priscus, and Heraclides son of Palmas, and Phib son of
11 Iulius, and the other komarchs of this (village), greeting. We acknowledge that we have received from
12 your glory as a loan, and have had measured out to us from the produce of the present
13 fourteenth indiction, for the sowing of our arouras for the crops of the
14 fifteenth indiction, with God's help, of uncleaned wheat, without the sifting allowance,
15 by the cancellus measure, two hundred artabas, which were also given to us through the heirs of the
16 late Menas son of Asclas, shipmaster of your same glorious house, total 200 artabas of wheat by the cancellus measure;
17 which wheat, new and sifted, by the cancellus measure by which we received it, we will of necessity
18 return to your glory, together with our rent, in the month of Payni
19 of the present year 227 (and) 196, of the same present fourteenth indiction,
20 from the new crops of the fifteenth indiction, with God's help, without delay, at the risk of
21 our property, which is pledged for this. The document, written in a single copy, is valid, and in answer to the formal question we have acknowledged it. ⳨
22 We, the community of the protokometai of the village of Takona of the Oxyrhynchite nome, through the aforesaid
23 persons named in it, (have made) this document to your glory, and (have received) the wheat, two hundred artabas,

25 and all that is written is agreeable to us as aforesaid, ⳨ and in answer to the formal question we have acknowledged
26 and ἀπελήσαμεν (meaning unclear). I, Aurelius Heraclides, scribe of the village of Takona, having been asked, wrote for them,
27 as they are illiterate. ⳨
28 ☧ Executed through me, Philoxenus. Phaophi 23, indiction 14 [...] ⳨

1 Copy. Year two of Nero Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus Imperator,
2 month Kaisareios, epagomenal day 3, in the city of Oxyrhynchus in the Thebaid.
3 Heracleia daughter of Heraclides, citizen, with her guardian Nicippus son of Nicippus,
4 of the deme Althaieus, acknowledges to Papontos son of Aphynchis alias Zoilus, (all) from the city of Oxyrhynchus,
5 in the street, that she has ceded to him the right to exact and recover two hundred drachmas of silver of imperial
6 and Ptolemaic coinage, which Heracleia herself
7 happens to have had ceded to her by a cession executed
8 through the daily register of the record office in Kaisareios of the present
9 second year of Nero Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus Imperator,
10 and which were lent by (blank) to Pnepheros son of Papontos, registered as
11 Persian of the epigone, by another cession executed
12 through the same record office on the epagomenal days of Kaisareios of the
13 first year of Nero Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus Imperator;
14 and that she has likewise also ceded to him the right of execution which she herself
15 was ceded through the cession made to her as aforesaid
16 of the two hundred drachmas of silver, [...]
17 [...] that she has ceded to him the right to exact and recover [...]
18 [...] of the 200 drachmas of silver and the interest, and to do everything else as
19 she herself and Irenaeus were entitled to do; and she has forthwith handed over to
20 Papontos the two cessions made to her and to Irenaeus as aforesaid,
21 which she will guarantee to be lawful and undischarged,
22 because she has been paid in full by Papontos the

24 is to be invalid, and further Heracleia or anyone
25 proceeding on her behalf is to pay to Papontos or his successors for each
26 claim the damages and a fine of one hundred drachmas of silver and

1 In the year after the second consulship of Flavius Eusebius, vir clarissimus, Choiak 2, indiction 4, in Oxyrhynchus.
2 To Flavius Apphous, vir clarissimus, tribune, son of Eulogius of excellent memory,
3 of the splendid and most splendid city of the Oxyrhynchites, Aurelius Theon son of Ioannes,
4 his mother being Heraclia, pastry-cook, of the same city, greeting. I acknowledge by this
5 my written security that I have received from you as a loan, from hand
6 out of your house, for my own pressing need, two single imperial
7 gold solidi of full weight, in number two, total 2 gold solidi, on condition that I supply and
8 give to your nobility as interest on them until the term stated below
9 the lawful hundredth interest on them without default,
10 which interest and the capital itself I will of necessity repay to your excellence:
11 one solidus in the month of Tybi of the present year 172 (and) 141 of the
12 present fourth indiction, with the interest, and the other in the
13 month of Hathyr of the coming year [173] (and) 142 of the fifth indiction, with God's help,
14 with the interest, without delay and without any dispute, lawsuit
15 or judgment; and that I may not, when each term has come,
16 delay the repayment or ask for another extension,
17 or say that I have paid anything of this debt without written
18 receipts and a joint receipt, or before the return of this
19 document of mine, but you shall have the right of exaction upon me and upon
20 all my property. The document,
21 written in a single copy, is valid, and to the formal question I have assented. I, Aurelius Theon son of Ioannes, pas-
22 try-cook, the aforesaid, have received the two gold solidi of capital and will re-
23 pay them at the terms with the interest, and everything written is agreeable to me
24 as aforesaid, and to the formal question I have assented and released (it). I, Apphouas, lector,
25 son of Philoxenus, at his request wrote for him, as he does not know letters.
26 ☧ Written through me, Thoth (?). Choiak 2, indiction 4.
(verso)
27 (? lines illegible)

Interest: the lawful hundredth interest (νόμιμον ἑκατοστιαῖον τόκον, l. 9), i.e. 1% per month.
Term: one solidus in Tybi of the present year (= December AD 495/January AD 496), the other in Hathyr of the next (= October/November AD 496), each with interest (ll. 10-14).
Date: Choiak 2, indiction 4 (= 29 November AD 495).

English translation:
(recto)
1 ⳨ In the reign of our most divine and most pious
2 master Flavius Justinian,
3 the eternal Augustus and Impera-
4 tor, year 27, in the 13th (year) after the
5 consulship of Flavius Basilius, vir clarissimus,
6 Payni 14, indiction 2.
7 To Flavius Anastasius, the
8 most admirable comes and
9 banker of the glorious house, of
10 the splendid city of the Oxyrhynchites,
11 the Aurelii Georgius and Anoup,
12 full brothers, of the father
13 Andreas, their mother being Stephanous,
14 machine-makers of the same glorious house,
15 of the same city, greeting.
16 We acknowledge that we have received from
17 your magnificence, at our
18 request, as a loan, from hand
19 out of its house, for our own and
20 pressing needs, four gold solidi
21 current on the private standard, total 4 gold solidi
22 current, and we acknowledge that we will re-
23 pay them to your magnificence with all
24 gratitude out of the first instalment of
25 our wages from the glorious house in the month of Hathyr
26 of the coming third indiction,
27 without delay, at the risk of our property,
28 pledged for this. The document, written in a single copy, is valid,
29 and in answer to the formal question we have assented. We, the Aurelii Georgius and
30 Anoup, sons of Andreas, have made the document
31 of the 4 solidi as aforesaid. I, Pamouthius son of Georgius,
32 at their request wrote for them, as they are illiterate.
33 ☧ Executed through me [...].
(verso)
34 ⳨ Document of Georgius and Anoup, brothers, of the father Andreas, machine-makers of the glorious house,
35 of the city of the Oxyrhynchites, 4 gold solidi current on the private standard. ⳨

Term: out of the first instalment of the borrowers' wages from the estate, in Hathyr of indiction 3 (= October/November AD 554) (ll. 22-26).
Date: Payni 14, indiction 2, year 27 of Justinian (= 8 June AD 554).

English translation:
(recto)
1 ⳨ In the reign of our most divine and most pious master Flavius
2 Tiberius Mauricius, eternal Augustus and Imperator,
3 year 1, after the consulship of our master of divine memory
4 Tiberius Constantine, year 4, Hathyr 27, indiction 1.
5 To the most magnificent heirs of Apion of glorious memory,
6 former first patrician, landowners also here
7 in the splendid city of the Oxyrhynchites, through Menas, servant, who
8 makes the stipulation and acquires for his own masters, the
9 same all-renowned men, the right of action and obligation, the Aurelii
10 Samuel son of Victor, his mother being Susanna, and Areotes son of
11 Phoebammon, his mother being Tsaeie, from the hamlet of
12 Melitas in the Oxyrhynchite nome, with their surety Georgius, their pronoetes,
13 son of the late Apollos, of the (city) of the Oxyrhynchites.
14 We acknowledge that we have received from your magnificence
15 here and now, for the sowing of the crops of the second
16 indiction, eleven artabas of wheat by the cancellus measure, as follows:
17 I, Areotes, six artabas, I, Samuel, the
18 other five artabas, total 11 artabas of wheat, and we acknowledge that we will
19 provide them to your magnificence at the time of the threshing
20 of the second indiction, or I, their surety, will give them on their behalf
21 from my own resources. The document, written in a single copy, is valid, and in answer to the formal question we have assented. We, the Aurelii
22 Areotes and Samuel, agree as aforesaid. I, Papnouthius, wrote
23 for them as they are illiterate. I, Georgius, pronoetes, son of the late Apollos, the aforesaid,
24 am surety for the same Samuel and Areotes in everything as aforesaid. ⳨
25 ☧ Executed through me, Papnouthius.
(verso)
26 ⳨ Document of Areotes and Phoebammon (sic) from the hamlet of Melitas,
27 with their surety Georgius, pronoetes, son of Apollos, 11 artabas of wheat by the cancellus measure.

Estate seed loan: wheat for the sowing of indiction 2, 6 artabas to Areotes and 5 to Samuel, with their pronoetes Georgius as surety (ll. 14-20).
Term: at the threshing of indiction 2 (summer AD 583) (ll. 19-20).
Date: Hathyr 27, indiction 1, year 1 of Maurice (= 23 November AD 582).

8 [a copy is appended.] Helene daughter of Aphelix, grandson of Psosnaus, her mother being Eudaemonis, with her guardian, who is also surety for
9 the payment of everything under this mortgage, her own son Diodorus alias Longinus son of Amois,
10 grandson of Diodorus, of Chysis, to Spartas son of Pausanias, grandson of Sarapion, his mother being Didyme, of the city of Oxyrhynchus, greeting. I acknow-
11 ledge that I have from you, of silver of imperial coinage, one thousand eight hundred drachmas of capital, to which nothing at
12 all has been added, at interest of three obols per mina per month from the present month of Mecheir to the month of
13 Hathyr (?) of the coming 12th year, amounting to one hundred and eighty-nine drachmas, and the total of capital and inter-
14 est, one thousand nine hundred and eighty-nine drachmas of silver, (I have) on the mortgage of catoecic grain-bearing sown land,
15 full, in a rectangle, of four arouras of what belongs to me near the same Chysis in the Hermopolite, land
16 on release, in the kleros of Pausanias, of five arouras which are among twenty arouras held in common and undivided
17 with Chesphibis son of Petosiris and others, of all of which the neighbours are south a field, north the heirs of Saturninus
18 and others, east the boundary of the kleroi, west the same heirs of Saturninus; and the total of one thousand
19 nine hundred and eighty-nine drachmas of silver I will repay to you or your representatives on the thirtieth of Phaophi of the coming
20 [12th year] of Antoninus Caesar the lord, Armeniacus Medicus Parthicus Maximus, without any delay;
21 if I do not repay as written, you shall own in place of these (sums) the aforesaid arouras and may
22 use and manage them in whatever way you choose, and I am obliged to guarantee them to you as secure at
23 all times against everyone with every guarantee and free from cultivation of royal land and of your estate land and of anything
24 else from now on, and whenever you wish you may register a notice of possession of the mortgage and of the same arou-
25 ras through the property record office of the Hermopolite, without needing
26 my presence or co-signature. If I contravene any of this, it is to be invalid and I will pay in addition, for
27 each kind of contravention, the damages and a fine of six hundred drachmas of silver and to the trea-
28 sury the same, the aforesaid remaining valid nonetheless, and the mortgage is valid,
29 written in two copies, alike, without erasure or insertion, in the own hand of me, Diodorus alias Longinus.
30 Year 10 of Imperator Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Armeniacus Medicus Parthicus Maximus,
31 Mecheir 24. I, Helene daughter of Aphelix, have from you, Spartas, the one thousand eight hundred drachmas at interest of three obols, amount-
